message.abstract: Crack segmentation supports surface-defect inspection and infrastructure health monitoring. However, cracks are often elongated, sparse, discontinuous, and multi-scale, with low contrast, blurred boundaries, and topology-sensitive structures. Complex textures, shadows, and weak responses can cause missed fine cracks, boundary displacement, and structural breaks. Although dual-branch convolutional neural network (CNN)-Mamba architectures combine local detail with global context, three limitations remain. Heterogeneous branches can be spatially misaligned, decoders may not recover continuous multi-scale structures and boundary details simultaneously, and region-based supervision provides limited constraints on boundary displacement, centreline breaks, and missed fine cracks. To address these limitations, we propose DA-MSRNet, a dual-branch CNN-Mamba network for crack segmentation that integrates spatial alignment, multi-scale structural reconstruction, and boundary-topology collaborative supervision to improve fine-grained segmentation. Specifically, the Deformable Alignment and Branch Fusion Guidance Module (DA-BFGM) predicts dynamic offsets to calibrate contextual features before fusion, improving spatial correspondence between local details and global semantics and reducing boundary misalignment and local structural breaks. The Multi-Scale Feature Reconstruction Module (MSFRM) strengthens decoder reconstruction of fine, discontinuous, and weak-response cracks through multi-scale directional modelling, channel-spatial recalibration, and edge enhancement. Boundary-Topology Collaborative Supervision (BTCS) jointly constrains region overlap, boundary localisation, skeleton connectivity, and missed detections to improve contour accuracy and structural continuity. Experiments on DeepCrack, CrackTree260, and the Crack Forest Dataset (CFD) show that DA-MSRNet achieves higher Recall, F1-score, and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) than seven comparison models. Its mIoU values are 88.11%, 85.97%, and 82.26%, respectively.
title: DA-MSRNet: A Dual-Branch CNN-Mamba Network with Deformable Alignment and Multi-Scale Feature Reconstruction for Crack Segmentation
